text: Though Mitya began speaking sternly, he apparently was trying all the more not to forget or skip over the least detail in his account.
explanation: Even though Mitya started his testimony with a serious tone, he seemed highly motivated to include every minor detail in his story.

text: He told how he had jumped over the fence into his father’s garden, how he went up to the window, and, finally, everything that took place under the window.
explanation: He narrated the events of his entry into his father's garden by jumping the fence, his approach to the window, and the subsequent actions he performed there.

text: Clearly, precisely, as though hammering it out, he spoke of the feelings that had troubled him during those moments in the garden, when he had wanted so terribly to know whether Grushenka was with his father or not.
explanation: He expressed the powerful emotional distress he felt while in the garden, particularly his intense desire to confirm if his mistress, Grushenka, was inside with his father, stating this with great force and clarity.

text: But, strangely, this time both the prosecutor and the district attorney somehow listened with terrible reserve, looked at him drily, asked far fewer questions.
explanation: Surprisingly, the prosecutor and the district attorney maintained a distant and cold demeanor, limiting their questions significantly.

text: Mitya could gather nothing from their faces.
explanation: Mitya was unable to interpret their neutral expressions to understand their thoughts.

text: “They’re angry and offended,” he thought, “well, devil take them!”
explanation: He mentally concluded that the officials were displeased or insulted, and he dismissed their feelings.

text: When he told how he finally made up his mind to give his father the signal that Grushenka had come, so that he would open the window, the prosecutor and the district attorney paid no attention to the word “signal,” as if they had no idea at all of the word’s significance here; Mitya even noticed it.
explanation: When Mitya described his decision to use a special 'signal' to trick his father into opening the window by suggesting Grushenka had arrived, the officials conspicuously ignored the key word "signal," prompting Mitya to observe their deliberate lack of interest.

text: When he finally came to the moment when, seeing his father leaning out of the window, hatred boiled up in him and he snatched the pestle from his pocket, he suddenly stopped as if on purpose.
explanation: When his narrative reached the point where his father appeared at the window, causing his hatred to surge and leading him to pull the pestle from his pocket, he abruptly paused his account.

text: He sat and looked at the wall, knowing they both had their eyes glued to him.
explanation: Mitya remained seated, gazing at the wall, aware that both the prosecutor and the district attorney were intently watching him.

text: “Well, sir,” said the district attorney, “so you snatched out the weapon and ... and what then?”
explanation: The district attorney prompted him to continue, asking what action followed the moment he drew the weapon.

text: “Then? Oh, then I killed him ... smashed him on the head and split his skull.
explanation: Mitya sarcastically responded by stating the assumed outcome: that he murdered his father by hitting him over the head and fracturing his skull.

text: That’s your version, is it!” he suddenly flashed his eyes.
explanation: He aggressively challenged the officials, asking if that violent act was the version they believed.

text: All the wrath that had almost died out in him suddenly rose up in his soul with extraordinary force.
explanation: The anger he had been suppressing instantly reignited within him with tremendous intensity.

text: “Ours,” Nikolai Parfenovich repeated, “well, and what is yours?”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich confirmed that was their version of events and then asked Mitya to present his own.

text: Mitya lowered his eyes and was silent for a long time.
explanation: Mitya looked down and did not speak for an extended period.

text: “My version, gentlemen, my version is this,” he began softly.
explanation: Mitya began to speak quietly, starting the presentation of his own account.

text: “Whether it was someone’s tears, or God heard my mother’s prayers, or a bright spirit kissed me at that moment, I don’t know—but the devil was overcome.
explanation: He attributed his change of heart to a spiritual or emotional intervention—perhaps tears, his mother's prayers, or a divine inspiration—which successfully defeated the evil impulse within him.

text: I dashed away from the window and ran to the fence. . .
explanation: Instead of striking his father, he rapidly fled from the window and headed toward the fence.

text: Father got frightened.
explanation: His father became terrified by his presence.

text: He caught sight of me then for the first time, cried out, and jumped back from the window—I remember that very well.
explanation: Mitya recalls vividly that his father finally saw him, screamed, and recoiled from the window.

text: And I ran through the garden to the fence ... it was here that Grigory caught up with me, when I was already sitting on the fence ...”
explanation: He continued running across the garden to the fence, which is where Grigory intercepted him while Mitya was perched on it.

text: At this point he finally raised his eyes to his listeners.
explanation: After finishing this part of his story, he looked up at the officials.

text: They seemed to be looking at him with completely untroubled attention.
explanation: The interrogators appeared to be listening calmly and without showing any sign of belief or disbelief.

text: A sort of twinge of indignation went through Mitya’s soul.
explanation: Mitya felt a sudden burst of anger or resentment because of their reserved reaction.

text: “But I see right now you’re laughing at me, gentlemen!” he suddenly interrupted.
explanation: He abruptly stopped talking and accused the officials of silently mocking him.

text: “Why would you draw such a conclusion?” Nikolai Parfenovich remarked.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich asked Mitya why he assumed they were making fun of him.

text: “You don’t believe a word of it, that’s why!
explanation: Mitya stated that the reason he concluded they were laughing was their obvious disbelief in his story.

text: I quite understand that I’ve come to the main point: the old man is now lying there with his head smashed in, and I—having tragically described how I wanted to kill him and how I already snatched out the pestle—I suddenly run away from the window ...
explanation: He acknowledged the central contradiction in his story: his father is dead from a head injury, and yet Mitya's account has him dramatically wanting to kill him and drawing the weapon, only to inexplicably run away.

text: A poem!
explanation: He sarcastically dismissed his own explanation as a dramatic, fictionalized piece of writing.

text: In verse!
explanation: He added that it sounded like a poetic fabrication.

text: Take the good man’s word for it!
explanation: He mocked the idea that they should simply accept his word as an honest man.

text: Ha, ha!
explanation: He laughed scornfully.

text: You are scoffers, gentlemen!”
explanation: He directly labeled the interrogators as mockers or skeptics.

text: And he swung his whole body around on the chair so hard that the chair creaked.
explanation: His agitation caused him to spin forcefully in his seat, making the chair loudly complain.

text: “And did you notice,” the prosecutor began suddenly, as if paying no attention to Mitya’s excitement, “did you notice, when you ran away from the window, whether the door to the garden, at the other end of the house, was open or not?”
explanation: The prosecutor abruptly changed the subject, ignoring Mitya's emotional outburst, and asked if Mitya had observed whether the garden door at the opposite end of the house was open when he fled the window.

text: “No, it was not open.”
explanation: Mitya stated that the door was definitely closed.

text: “It was not?”
explanation: The prosecutor repeated the denial, questioning the certainty of Mitya's memory.

text: “On the contrary, it was shut.
explanation: Mitya firmly reiterated that the door was closed.

text: Who could have opened it?
explanation: He wondered who might have been able to open the door.

text: Bah, the door— wait!” he suddenly seemed to collect himself and all but jumped up.
explanation: He paused his thoughts about the door, instantly becoming focused and nearly rising from his seat.

text: “Did you find the door open?”
explanation: He asked the investigators if they had discovered the door to be open.

text: “Open.”
explanation: The prosecutor simply confirmed that the door was open.

text: “But who could have opened it, if you didn’t open it yourselves?”
explanation: Mitya was extremely surprised and questioned how the door could have been open since he claimed not to have done it, and implying they had no reason to.

text: Mitya was suddenly terribly surprised.
explanation: Mitya's shock at the revelation was profound.

text: “The door was open, and your father’s murderer undoubtedly went in through that door and, having committed the murder, went out through the same door,” the prosecutor spoke slowly and distinctly, as though hammering out each word.
explanation: The prosecutor forcefully and deliberately stated their conclusion: that the killer used the open door to enter, commit the murder, and then exit.

text: “It is perfectly clear to us.
explanation: He asserted that this sequence of events was unequivocally established in their minds.

text: The murder obviously took place , in the room, and not through the window, which is positively clear from the investigation carried out, from the position of the body, and everything else.
explanation: He explained that the investigation, including the victim's body position, confirmed that the murder happened inside the room, not through the window.

text: There can be no doubt of that circumstance.”
explanation: The prosecutor insisted that there was absolute certainty regarding the murder taking place inside the room.

text: Mitya was terribly astounded.
explanation: Mitya was completely overwhelmed and confused by this new information.

text: “But that’s impossible, gentlemen!” he cried out, completely at a loss.
explanation: Mitya shouted that this was completely unbelievable, expressing his total confusion.

text: “I ... I didn’t go in . . .I tell you positively, with exactness, that the door was shut all the while I was in the garden and when I ran out of the garden.
explanation: He insisted firmly and with certainty that he never entered the house and that the door remained closed during his entire time in the garden and his departure.

text: I just stood outside the window and saw him in the window, and that’s all, that’s all ...
explanation: He maintained that his only action was standing outside, looking at his father through the window.

text: I remember it down to the last moment.
explanation: He claimed his memory of the events was absolutely complete and accurate.

text: And even if I didn’t remember, I know it anyway, because the signals were known only to me and Smerdyakov, and to him, the dead man, and without the signals he wouldn’t have opened the door to anyone in the world.”
explanation: Mitya argued that regardless of his memory, he knew his father would not have opened the door to anyone without the secret signals, which were only known to himself, Smerdyakov, and the deceased.

text: “Signals?
explanation: The prosecutor seized on this word.

text: What kind of signals?” the prosecutor said with greedy, almost hysterical curiosity, and instantly lost all his reserved demeanor.
explanation: The prosecutor's desire to know about these signals was intense, causing him to immediately abandon his formal, reserved attitude.

text: He asked as if creeping up timidly.
explanation: He inquired cautiously, like someone approaching something fragile.

text: He scented an important fact, still unknown to him, and at once felt great fear that Mitya might not be willing to reveal it fully.
explanation: The prosecutor recognized the potential importance of this detail and immediately feared Mitya might withhold the full information.

text: “So you didn’t even know?” Mitya winked at him, smiling mockingly and spitefully.
explanation: Mitya gave him a malicious wink and a derisive smile, revealing that the officials were ignorant of this key information.

text: “And what if I won’t tell you?
explanation: He challenged the prosecutor, asking what they would do if he refused to disclose the details.

text: Who will you find out from then?
explanation: He pointed out that the only other people who knew were the dead man and Smerdyakov, making the information hard to acquire.

text: Only the dead man knew about the signals, and me, and Smerdyakov, that’s all, and heaven knew, too, but it won’t tell you.
explanation: Mitya reiterated that the knowledge was restricted to his dead father, himself, Smerdyakov, and God, who would not share the secret.

text: And it’s a curious little fact, one could build devil knows what on it, ha, ha!
explanation: He found the information fascinating and potent, suggesting its significance could lead to wild speculation, and he laughed scornfully.

text: Take comfort, gentlemen, I’ll reveal it to you.
explanation: He assured them, patronizingly, that he would eventually share the secret.

text: You’ve got foolishness in your minds.
explanation: He accused them of having mistaken or foolish beliefs.

text: You don’t know with whom you’re dealing!
explanation: He claimed they did not understand his true character.

text: You’re dealing with a suspect who gives evidence against himself, who gives evidence that does him harm!
explanation: He proudly declared that he was a suspect who voluntarily offered testimony that was self-incriminating.

text: Yes, sirs, for I am a knight of honor and you are not!”
explanation: He asserted his moral superiority by claiming he possessed a code of honor that they lacked.

text: The prosecutor swallowed all these pills; he was simply trembling with impatience to know about the new fact.
explanation: The prosecutor endured Mitya's insults, focused only on his desperate eagerness to hear the new, crucial detail.

text: Mitya gave them a precise and extensive account of everything to do with the signals invented by Fyodor Pavlovich for Smerdyakov, told them precisely what each knock on the window meant, even knocked out the signals on the table, and when asked by Nikolai Parfenovich whether it meant that he, Mitya, when he knocked on the old man’s window, had used precisely the signal meaning “Grushenka has come,” answered exactly that, yes, he had used precisely the signal meaning “Grushenka has come.”
explanation: Mitya then provided a detailed and thorough description of the signals Fyodor Pavlovich created for Smerdyakov, explaining the meaning of each window knock, demonstrating them on the table, and confirming to Nikolai Parfenovich that the signal he used was the one that meant "Grushenka has come."

text: “There you are, now build your tower!” Mitya broke off, and again turned away from them in contempt.
explanation: Mitya finished his explanation, contemptuously challenging the officials to make a case using this information, and physically turned away from them once more.

text: “And only your deceased parent, you, and the servant Smerdyakov knew about these signals?
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich sought final confirmation that the only people aware of the signals were the victim, Mitya, and the servant Smerdyakov.

text: And no one else?” Nikolai Parfenovich inquired once again.
explanation: He repeated the question to ensure there were no other persons involved.

text: “Yes, the servant Smerdyakov, and heaven, too.
explanation: Mitya confirmed the list, mockingly adding heaven.

text: Write that down about heaven, too; it’s worth writing down.
explanation: He insisted that they document the detail about heaven, suggesting its importance.

text: And you’ll have need of God yourselves.”
explanation: He made a final cryptic remark suggesting they, too, would eventually require divine assistance.

text: Of course, they began writing it down, but while they were writing, the prosecutor, as if stumbling quite unexpectedly onto a new thought, suddenly said:
explanation: The investigators started documenting the information, and in the middle of this process, the prosecutor quickly voiced a spontaneous new idea.

text: “But if Smerdyakov also knew about these signals, and you radically deny all accusations of your father’s death, then was it not he who, having given the agreed signal, got your father to unlock the door for him, and then ... committed the crime?”
explanation: The prosecutor posed a question: given that Smerdyakov knew the signals and Mitya denied the murder, was it possible that Smerdyakov used the signal to make the father unlock the door and then proceeded to commit the murder?

text: Mitya gave him a deeply mocking and at the same time terribly hateful look.
explanation: Mitya stared at the prosecutor with a look that was both highly scornful and intensely hostile.

text: He stared at him long and silently, until the prosecutor began blinking his eyes.
explanation: Mitya held the intimidating stare for a prolonged time until the prosecutor grew uncomfortable and started blinking.

text: “Caught the fox again!” Mitya spoke finally.
explanation: Mitya finally spoke, triumphantly suggesting he had exposed the prosecutor's scheme.

text: “Pinched the rascal by the tail, heh, heh!
explanation: He used another metaphor to say he had caught the prosecutor in a cunning move, accompanied by a laugh.

text: I see right through you, prosecutor!
explanation: Mitya claimed he could easily understand the prosecutor's motives and strategy.

text: You thought I’d jump up at once, snatch your prompting, and shout at the top of my lungs: ‘Aie, it’s Smerdyakov, he’s the murderer! ‘
explanation: He correctly guessed that the prosecutor had intended to trick him into immediately naming Smerdyakov as the killer.

text: Admit that’s what you thought, admit it, and then I’ll go on.”
explanation: Mitya demanded that the prosecutor confess to this intention before he would continue his testimony.

text: But the prosecutor admitted nothing.
explanation: The prosecutor refused to confirm Mitya's theory.

text: He was silent and waited.
explanation: He remained quiet, expecting Mitya to speak next.

text: “You’re mistaken, I will not shout against Smerdyakov!” said Mitya.
explanation: Mitya told the prosecutor that his assumption was wrong, and he would not rashly accuse Smerdyakov.

text: “And you do not even suspect him at all?”
explanation: The prosecutor asked if Mitya had absolutely no suspicion of Smerdyakov.

text: “Do you suspect him? “
explanation: Mitya countered by asking if the prosecutor himself suspected Smerdyakov.

text: “He is one of our suspects.”
explanation: The prosecutor admitted that Smerdyakov was included among their list of suspects.

text: Mitya planted his eyes on the floor.
explanation: Mitya looked down intensely at the floor.

text: “Joking aside,” he said gloomily, “listen: from the very beginning, almost from the moment when I ran out to you from behind the curtains tonight, this thought already flashed through me: ‘Smerdyakov! ‘
explanation: Mitya began speaking seriously, revealing that the idea of Smerdyakov being the killer had occurred to him almost immediately that night.

text: All the while I was sitting here at the table, shouting that I was not guilty of blood, I kept thinking: ‘Smerdyakov!’
explanation: Even while passionately proclaiming his innocence, the suspicion of Smerdyakov persisted in his mind.

text: And Smerdyakov would not let go of my soul.
explanation: The thought of Smerdyakov being the murderer continuously troubled his conscience.

text: Finally, just now I suddenly had the same thought: ‘Smerdyakov,’ but only for a second; immediately, right next to it, came the thought: ‘No, not Smerdyakov! ‘
explanation: The thought of Smerdyakov recurred just now, but was instantly replaced by an equally strong conviction that Smerdyakov was not the culprit.

text: It’s not his doing, gentlemen.”
explanation: Mitya concluded definitively that Smerdyakov was not responsible for the murder.

text: “In that case, do you suspect yet another person?” Nikolai Parfenovich asked guardedly.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich cautiously asked if Mitya suspected any person other than himself or Smerdyakov.

text: “I don’t know who or what person, the hand of heaven or Satan, but. . not Smerdyakov!” Mitya snapped out resolutely.
explanation: Mitya responded with certainty that he didn't know who or what supernatural force was responsible, but he was absolutely sure it was not Smerdyakov.

text: “But why do you maintain so firmly and with such insistence that he is not the one?”
explanation: The prosecutor asked for the reasons behind Mitya's unwavering certainty that Smerdyakov was innocent.

text: “From conviction.
explanation: Mitya's certainty stemmed from an inner belief.

text: From impression.
explanation: It was also based on his personal perception of the man.

text: Because Smerdyakov is a man of the most abject nature and a coward.
explanation: His primary reason was Smerdyakov's fundamentally base character and extreme timidity.

text: Not just a coward, but a conjunction of all cowardice in the world taken together, walking on two legs.
explanation: Mitya graphically described Smerdyakov as the very embodiment of global cowardice.

text: He was born of a chicken.
explanation: Mitya used an insulting term to emphasize Smerdyakov's extreme lack of courage.

text: Every time he talked with me, he trembled for fear I might kill him, though I never even raised my hand.
explanation: Mitya stated that Smerdyakov was so fearful of him that he would shake in Mitya's presence, even when Mitya made no threatening gestures.

text: He fell at my feet and wept, he kissed these very boots of mine, literally, begging me not to ‘scare’ him.
explanation: Smerdyakov would fall down, cry, and physically kiss Mitya's boots, pleading with Mitya to stop "scaring" him.

text: ‘Scare,’ do you hear?—what sort of word is that?
explanation: Mitya drew attention to the passive, childlike nature of the word Smerdyakov used.

text: And I even gave him presents.
explanation: Mitya mentioned that he had given Smerdyakov gifts.

text: He’s a sickly, epileptic, feebleminded chicken, who could be thrashed by an eight-year-old boy.
explanation: He summarized Smerdyakov's physical and mental state as frail, epileptic, simple-minded, and so weak that a child could beat him.

text: What sort of a character is that?
explanation: Mitya questioned how such a weak individual could commit a murder.

text: No, not Smerdyakov, gentlemen—and he doesn’t care about money either, he never would take my presents ...
explanation: Mitya reiterated Smerdyakov's innocence, adding that the man had no interest in money and refused his gifts.

text: Anyway,why would he kill the old man?
explanation: He questioned Smerdyakov's motive for murdering Fyodor Pavlovich.

text: You see he may be his son, his natural son, do you know that?”
explanation: Mitya asked the officials if they were aware of the common belief that Smerdyakov was Fyodor Pavlovich's illegitimate son.

text: “We have heard that legend.
explanation: The prosecutor acknowledged that they had been informed of the story concerning Smerdyakov's parentage.

text: But after all, you, too, are your father’s son, and yet you told everyone you wanted to kill him.”
explanation: The prosecutor drew a parallel, pointing out that Mitya was also the victim's son, and Mitya himself had publicly expressed the desire to murder his father.

text: “A rock through my own window!
explanation: Mitya referred to his own violent behavior, accepting the metaphor.

text: And a low one, a nasty one!
explanation: He agreed that the prosecutor's comparison was a despicable and mean-spirited comment.

text: I’m not afraid.
explanation: He stated that he was not intimidated by their accusation.

text: Oh, gentlemen, how mean of you to say that to my face!
explanation: Mitya exclaimed that it was a cruel and base thing for them to say directly to him.

text: Mean, because I myself said it to you.
explanation: He argued that it was mean precisely because he had been honest and confessed his murderous intent to them voluntarily.

text: I not only wanted to kill him, but I could well have killed him, and I voluntarily heaped it upon myself that I almost killed him!
explanation: He admitted that he not only wished to kill his father but was capable of it, and that he had freely confessed to almost committing the act.

text: But I didn’t kill him, my guardian angel saved me—that’s what you haven’t taken into consideration ...
explanation: He emphatically stated that he did not commit the murder, attributing his restraint to divine intervention, a fact he accused them of ignoring.

text: And that is what makes it mean, mean!
explanation: He repeated that their meanness lay in overlooking the fact that he was innocent.

text: Because I didn’t kill him, I didn’t, I didn’t!
explanation: He cried out a triple denial of committing the murder.

text: Do you hear, prosecutor: I didn’t!”
explanation: He demanded the prosecutor acknowledge his denial.

text: He almost choked.
explanation: Mitya was so overcome with emotion that he struggled to breathe.

text: Not once during the whole investigation had he been so agitated.
explanation: His emotional state was the most intensely agitated it had been throughout the entire interrogation process.

text: “And what has he told you, gentlemen—Smerdyakov, I mean?” he suddenly concluded, after a silence.
explanation: Following a pause, Mitya abruptly changed the topic to ask the officials what Smerdyakov's testimony was.

text: “May I ask you that?”
explanation: He asked for permission to inquire about Smerdyakov's statement.

text: “You may ask us anything,” the prosecutor replied with a cold and stern look, “anything concerning the factual side of the case, and it is our duty, I repeat, to satisfy your every question.
explanation: The prosecutor, looking serious and detached, informed Mitya that he was entitled to ask questions related to the facts of the case, and they were obligated to answer them.

text: We found the servant Smerdyakov, about whom you inquire, lying unconscious in his bed with a very severe attack of the falling sickness, which had recurred perhaps ten times in succession.
explanation: The prosecutor reported that Smerdyakov was discovered lying unconscious due to a severe epileptic fit the falling sickness that had repeated itself many times.

text: The doctor who was with us examined the sick man and told us he might not even live till morning.”
explanation: He added that the doctor who accompanied them believed Smerdyakov was so ill that he might die before dawn.

text: “Well, in that case the devil killed my father!” suddenly escaped from Mitya, as if even up to that minute he had been asking himself: “Smerdyakov, or not Smerdyakov?”
explanation: Mitya burst out that, if Smerdyakov was incapacitated, then a supernatural force must have committed the murder, revealing that he had been internally debating Smerdyakov's guilt until that very moment.

text: “We shall return to this fact again,” Nikolai Parfenovich resolved, “and now wouldn’t you like to go on with your evidence?”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich decided they would address Smerdyakov's condition later, asking Mitya to resume his testimony for now.

text: Mitya asked for a rest.
explanation: Mitya requested a break from the interrogation.

text: It was politely granted.
explanation: The break was courteously permitted.

text: Having rested, he began to go on.
explanation: After taking the break, Mitya recommenced his account.

text: But it was obviously difficult for him.
explanation: Continuing the testimony was clearly a struggle for him.

text: He was worn out, insulted, and morally shaken.
explanation: He was exhausted physically, felt personally attacked, and was emotionally destabilized.

text: Besides, the prosecutor, now quite intentionally, began irritating him every moment by pestering him with “details.”
explanation: Additionally, the prosecutor deliberately started to provoke him by insisting on minute and annoying "details" at every turn.

text: As soon as Mitya described how, sitting astride the fence, he had hit Grigory, who was clutching his left leg, on the head with the pestle, and then jumped down at once to the stricken man, the prosecutor stopped him and asked him to describe in greater detail how he was sitting on the fence.
explanation: When Mitya described striking Grigory who was holding his left leg on the head with the pestle while straddling the fence, and then immediately jumping down, the prosecutor interrupted to ask for a more detailed account of Mitya's posture on the fence.

text: Mitya was surprised.
explanation: Mitya was taken aback by the request for such trivial information.

text: “Well, like this, astride it, one leg here, the other there...”
explanation: He explained that he was straddling the fence with one leg on either side.

text: “And the pestle?”
explanation: The prosecutor asked where the pestle was at that moment.

text: “The pestle was in my hand.”
explanation: Mitya replied that he was holding the pestle.

text: “Not in your pocket?
explanation: The prosecutor asked if it was possible it was not in his pocket.

text: You remember such a detail?
explanation: The prosecutor highlighted Mitya's memory of this specific detail.

text: So, then you must have swung hard?”
explanation: The prosecutor inferred that Mitya must have used a strong, deliberate motion to hit Grigory.

text: “I must have swung hard—but what do you need that for?”
explanation: Mitya agreed that he must have struck forcefully, but questioned the relevance of the detail to the investigation.

text: “Why don’t you sit on the chair exactly as you were sitting on the fence then, and act out for us visually, for the sake of clarification, how and where you swung, in what direction?”
explanation: The prosecutor requested that Mitya physically reenact the scene, sitting on the chair as if it were the fence, to visually demonstrate the direction and manner of his swing.

text: “You’re not mocking me, are you?” Mitya asked, glancing haughtily at his interrogator, but the latter did not even bat an eye.
explanation: Mitya asked if the request was an attempt to ridicule him, looking scornfully at the prosecutor, who maintained a completely impassive expression.

text: Mitya turned convulsively, sat astride the chair, and swung his arm:
explanation: Mitya obeyed with a jerky, agitated movement, straddled the chair, and demonstrated the swing of his arm.

text: “That’s how I hit him!
explanation: Mitya stated that was the manner in which he struck Grigory.

text: That’s how I killed him!
explanation: He added, hyperbolically, that was how he killed him.

text: Anything else?”
explanation: He impatiently asked if there were any further ridiculous questions.

text: “Thank you.
explanation: The prosecutor thanked him for the demonstration.

text: Now may I trouble you to explain why, in fact, you jumped down, with what purpose, and what, in fact, you had in mind?”
explanation: The prosecutor then asked Mitya to explain his actual reason for jumping down to the fallen Grigory, his intention, and his thoughts at that time.

text: “Ah, the devil ... I jumped down to the stricken man ... I don’t know why!”
explanation: Mitya was exasperated and stated that he descended to the injured man but could not recall his exact reason for doing so.

text: “Even though you were so agitated?
explanation: The prosecutor pressed him, emphasizing his emotional state.

text: And running away?”
explanation: He also highlighted that Mitya was in the process of fleeing the scene.

text: “Yes, agitated and running away.”
explanation: Mitya confirmed he was agitated and running away when he jumped down.

text: “Did you want to help him?”
explanation: The prosecutor suggested that Mitya's intention might have been to aid the man.

text: “Help him, hah...!
explanation: Mitya scoffed at the idea of helping him.

text: Well, maybe also to help him, I forget.”
explanation: He then conceded that perhaps helping him was a secondary motivation, but he couldn't remember clearly.

text: “You forgot yourself?
explanation: The prosecutor asked if Mitya meant he had lost control of his own actions or thoughts.

text: That is, you were even somehow unconscious?”
explanation: The prosecutor further suggested that Mitya might have been temporarily unaware of his actions.

text: “Oh, no, not unconscious at all, I remember everything.
explanation: Mitya strongly denied being unconscious, stating he remembered everything clearly.

text: To the last shred.
explanation: He emphasized his memory was perfectly complete.

text: I jumped down to look at him and wiped the blood off with my handkerchief. “
explanation: Mitya specified that he jumped down to look at Grigory and used his handkerchief to wipe away the blood.

text: “We have seen your handkerchief.
explanation: The prosecutor confirmed they had possession of Mitya's bloody handkerchief.

text: Did you hope to bring the man you struck back to life?”
explanation: The prosecutor questioned if Mitya had hoped to revive the man he had injured.

text: “I don’t know if I hoped anything.
explanation: Mitya replied he didn't know if he had any specific hope.

text: I simply wanted to make sure if he was alive or not.”
explanation: He clarified that his goal was merely to check if the injured man was dead or alive.

text: “Ah, you wanted to make sure?
explanation: The prosecutor registered and focused on the motive of wanting to check.

text: Well, and so?”
explanation: He asked what Mitya concluded after checking.

text: “I’m not a doctor, I couldn’t tell.
explanation: Mitya replied that he lacked the medical expertise to determine Grigory's condition.

text: I ran away thinking I’d killed him, but he recovered.”
explanation: He admitted he fled believing he had murdered Grigory, though the man ultimately survived.

text: “Wonderful, sir,” the prosecutor concluded.
explanation: The prosecutor ironically praised Mitya's final statement.

text: “Thank you.
explanation: He thanked Mitya for his cooperation.

text: That is just what I wanted.
explanation: The prosecutor stated that this specific piece of information was exactly what he was attempting to obtain.

text: Be so good as to continue.”
explanation: He asked Mitya to resume his account.

text: Alas, it did not even occur to Mitya to tell them, though he remembered it, that he had jumped down out of pity, and that standing over the murdered man he had even uttered a few pathetic words: “You came a cropper, old man—there’s no help for it—now lie there.”
explanation: The narrator points out that Mitya, despite remembering his genuine pity and his tender words to the man—"You came a cropper, old man—there’s no help for it—now lie there”—did not mention these details to the interrogators.

text: But the prosecutor drew just one conclusion, that the man would only have jumped down “at such a moment and in such agitation,” with the purpose of making completely sure whether the sole witness to his crime was alive or not.
explanation: The prosecutor, however, concluded that Mitya's only possible motivation for jumping down while agitated was to ensure that the single person who had witnessed the attack was dead.

text: And what strength, consequently, what resolution, cold-bloodedness, and calculation the man possessed even at such a moment ... and so on and so forth.
explanation: The prosecutor's further conclusion was that this action proved Mitya had great inner strength, determination, emotional detachment, and planning ability, even during a frantic moment.

text: The prosecutor was pleased: “I irritated the morbid fellow with ‘details’ and he gave himself away.”
explanation: The prosecutor was satisfied because he believed his strategy of bothering the agitated Mitya with petty details had successfully exposed Mitya's true, calculated intent.

text: Painfully, Mitya went on.
explanation: Mitya resumed his testimony with evident difficulty and emotional distress.

text: But again he was stopped at once, this time by Nikolai Parfenovich:
explanation: He was immediately interrupted once more, but this time the question came from Nikolai Parfenovich.

text: “How could you have run to the servant, Fedosya Markov, with your hands and, as it turned out later, your face so covered with blood?”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich questioned how Mitya could have gone to the servant, Fedosya Markov, with his hands and—as subsequent findings showed—his face heavily stained with blood.

text: “But I didn’t notice at the time that there was any blood on me!” Mitya answered.
explanation: Mitya replied that he was completely unaware of the blood on his person at the time.

text: “That’s plausible, it does happen that way,” the prosecutor exchanged looks with Nikolai Parfenovich.
explanation: The prosecutor and Nikolai Parfenovich silently agreed that Mitya's explanation of not noticing the blood was believable, as such things can occur under stress.

text: “I precisely didn’t notice—beautiful, prosecutor,” Mitya, too, suddenly approved.
explanation: Mitya ironically praised the prosecutor for accepting the fact that he genuinely failed to notice the blood.

text: But next came the story of Mitya’s sudden decision “to remove himself” and “ make way for the happy ones. “
explanation: His narrative then moved to his sudden resolve to take his own life and clear the path for Grushenka and her former lover the "happy ones".

text: And now it was quite impossible for him to bring himself to lay bare his heart, as before, and tell them about “the queen of his soul.”
explanation: Mitya found he could no longer open up emotionally and speak candidly about his passionate love, which he called "the queen of his soul."

text: It sickened him in the face of these cold people, who “bit at him like bedbugs.”
explanation: The interrogators' coldness and their constant, irritating questioning likened to being bitten by bedbugs made him feel disgusted and unable to share intimate feelings.

text: Therefore, to their repeated questions, he declared briefly and sharply:
explanation: As a result of this distaste, his answers to their persistent questions were abrupt and concise.

text: “So I decided to kill myself.
explanation: Mitya stated that his final decision was suicide.

text: Why should I go on living?
explanation: He justified this decision by questioning his reason for living.

text: Naturally that jumped into the picture.
explanation: He claimed suicide was an obvious solution in his situation.

text: Her offender arrived, the former, indisputable one, and he came riding to her with love, after five years, to end the offense with legal marriage.
explanation: He explained that the man who had previously wronged Grushenka, the undeniable rival, had returned after a five-year absence, intending to marry her and correct the past wrong.

text: So I realized that it was all over for me ...
explanation: This arrival made him understand that his romantic prospects were finished.

text: And behind me was disgrace, and that blood, Grigory’s blood ...
explanation: He also felt burdened by dishonor and the guilt of injuring Grigory.

text: Why live?
explanation: He repeated the fundamental question of why he should continue living.

text: So I went to redeem the pawned pistols, to load them, and to put a bullet into my sconce at dawn ...”
explanation: He described his actions: retrieving his pawned pistols, loading them, and planning to shoot himself in the head at daybreak.

text: “And feast the night before?”
explanation: The prosecutor sarcastically asked if he planned to have a party the night before his suicide.

text: “And feast the night before.
explanation: Mitya confirmed he did plan to feast that night.

text: Eh, the devil, let’s get it over with quicker, gentlemen.
explanation: Mitya showed his impatience, wanting to rush through the rest of the account.

text: I was certainly going to shoot myself, not far from here, just outside town, and I would have disposed of myself at about five o’clock in the morning—I had a note all prepared in my pocket, I wrote it at Perkhotin’s when I loaded the pistol.
explanation: Mitya stated his definite plan to commit suicide near the town limits at around five in the morning, adding that he had prepared a suicide note while loading the pistol at Perkhotin’s house.

text: Here it is, read it.
explanation: He offered the note to them for reading.

text: I’m not telling it for you!” he suddenly added contemptuously.
explanation: He scornfully emphasized that he was not sharing the note for their benefit.

text: He threw the piece of paper from his waistcoat pocket onto the table in front of them; the investigators read it with curiosity, and, as is customary, filed it away,
explanation: He tossed the note from his waistcoat onto the table, and the officials read it out of interest before filing it as part of the case record.

text: “And you still did not think of washing your hands even as you entered Mr. Perkhotin’s?
explanation: The prosecutor asked why Mitya hadn't thought to wash his hands before entering Mr. Perkhotin's house.

text: In other words, you were not afraid of arousing suspicion?”
explanation: He suggested this lack of action meant Mitya was indifferent to the possibility of making people suspicious.

text: “What suspicion?
explanation: Mitya asked what kind of suspicion the prosecutor was referring to.

text: Suspicion or not, all the same I’d have driven here and shot myself at five o’clock, and there would have been no time to do anything about it.
explanation: He argued that suspicion was irrelevant because he was planning to drive to the site and kill himself at five o'clock, leaving no time for the authorities to act.

text: If it weren’t for what happened to my father, you wouldn’t have found anything out and come here.
explanation: He claimed that the only reason the investigators were present was the murder of his father.

text: Oh, the devil did it, the devil killed my father, and the devil let you find out so soon!
explanation: Mitya vehemently blamed the devil for both the murder and the investigators' unusually rapid discovery of the crime.

text: How on earth did you get here so soon?
explanation: He expressed profound surprise at the speed of their arrival.

text: It’s a wonder, fantastic!”
explanation: He declared their promptness to be miraculous and unbelievable.

text: “Mr. Perkhotin told us that when you came to him, you were holding your money ... a lot of money ... a wad of hundred-rouble bills ... in your hands ... your blood-stained hands, and that the servant boy also saw it!”
explanation: The prosecutor quoted Mr. Perkhotin's testimony, stating that Mitya arrived with his bloody hands openly clutching a large bundle of money in hundred-rouble notes, a sight witnessed also by the servant boy.

text: “Yes, gentlemen, that’s true, I remember.”
explanation: Mitya admitted that the prosecutor's account of his bloody hands and the money was accurate.

text: “Now one little question arises.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich stated that this information led to a minor, though significant, question.

text: Would you mind informing us,” Nikolai Parfenovich began with extreme gentleness, “as to where you suddenly got so much money, when it appears from the evidence, even from the simple reckoning of time, that you did not stop at your own lodgings?”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich, speaking very softly, asked Mitya to explain the source of the large sum of money, noting that based on the evidence and timeline, Mitya had not returned to his own residence.

text: The prosecutor winced slightly at the bluntness with which the question had been put, but he did not interrupt Nikolai Parfenovich.
explanation: The prosecutor briefly showed discomfort with the district attorney's directness but allowed him to continue.

text: “No, I didn’t stop at my lodgings,” Mitya replied, apparently very calmly, but dropping his eyes.
explanation: Mitya confirmed that he had not visited his own lodgings, speaking with an outward show of composure despite looking down.

text: “Allow me, in that case, to repeat the question,” Nikolai Parfenovich continued, somehow creeping up.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich pressed Mitya further, asking the question again, with a persistent, sneaky persistence.

text: “Where could you have gotten such a sum all at once, when, by your own admission, at five o’clock that same afternoon you...”
explanation: He rephrased the core issue: where Mitya could have instantly acquired so much money when he himself admitted that only hours earlier that day...

text: “Needed ten roubles, and pawned my pistols to Perkhotin, then went to Khokhlakov for three thousand, which she didn’t give me, and so on, and all the rest of it,” Mitya interrupted sharply.
explanation: Mitya quickly cut him off, listing his earlier financial distress: needing ten roubles, pawning his pistols, unsuccessfully trying to borrow three thousand from Madame Khokhlakov, and other related struggles.

text: “So, yes, gentlemen, I needed money, and then suddenly thousands appeared, eh?
explanation: Mitya acknowledged the contradiction: he was broke, and then suddenly appeared with thousands of roubles.

text: You know, gentlemen, you’re both afraid now: what if he won’t tell us where he got it?
explanation: He declared that he knew the investigators were worried that he would refuse to reveal the source of the money.

text: And so it is: I won’t tell you, gentlemen, you’ve guessed right, you’ll never know,” Mitya suddenly hammered out with great determination.
explanation: Mitya firmly and resolutely confirmed their fear, stating he would not disclose the source and they would never find out.

text: The investigators fell silent for a moment.
explanation: The interrogators paused, reacting to Mitya's determined refusal.

text: “Understand, Mr. Karamazov, that it is an essential necessity that we know this,” Nikolai Parfenovich said softly and humbly.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich spoke gently, urging Mitya to understand that this information was absolutely vital to the case.

text: “I understand, but I still won’t tell you.”
explanation: Mitya accepted the importance of the question but maintained his refusal to answer.

text: The prosecutor intervened and again reminded him that a man under interrogation was of course at liberty not to answer questions if he thought it more beneficial, and so on, but in view of the harm the suspect might do himself by keeping silent, and especially in view of questions of such importance as . . .
explanation: The prosecutor took over, repeating the standard advisory that a suspect has the right to refuse to answer questions if they believe it serves their interest, but cautioned Mitya about the serious self-harm caused by remaining silent on such a critical question.

text: “And so on, gentlemen, and so on!
explanation: Mitya impatiently dismissed the rest of the prosecutor's legalistic speech.

text: Enough, I’ve heard the whole harangue before!” Mitya again interrupted.
explanation: He cut off the prosecutor, stating that he had heard the entire lengthy speech already.

text: “I myself understand the importance of the matter and what the most essential point is, and I still won’t tell you.”
explanation: Mitya asserted that he fully grasped the crucial nature of the question but remained firm in his refusal to answer it.

text: “What is it to us, sir?
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich defensively asked why Mitya's refusal should concern them directly.

text: It’s not our business, but yours.
explanation: He argued that Mitya's decision to stay silent was detrimental only to Mitya himself.

text: You will only be harming yourself,” Nikolai Parfenovich remarked nervously.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich nervously stated that Mitya was merely causing self-harm.

text: “You see, gentlemen, joking aside,” Mitya raised his eyes and looked at them both steadily, “from the very beginning I had a feeling we would be at loggerheads on this point.
explanation: Mitya, looking them straight in the eye, said seriously that he had anticipated a fundamental disagreement on this particular matter since the interrogation began.

text: But when I first started giving evidence today, that was all in a fog of things to come, it was all floating out there, and I was even so naive as to make a suggestion of ‘mutual trust between us.’
explanation: He admitted that when he first started, the future conflict was unclear, and he had been foolish enough to suggest they could operate on a basis of mutual trust.

text: Now I see for myself that there could be no such trust, because we were bound to come to this cursed fence!
explanation: He realized that trust was impossible because they were destined to reach this unavoidable obstacle the "cursed fence" in the investigation.

text: Well, so we’ve come to it!
explanation: He stated that they have now arrived at that point of contention.

text: It’s impossible, that’s all!
explanation: He concluded that revealing the information was simply not an option.

text: I don’t blame you, by the way, it’s also impossible for you to take my word for it, I quite understand that.”
explanation: Mitya conceded that he did not hold the officials responsible for their skepticism, acknowledging that they couldn't simply accept his unsupported denial.

text: He fell gloomily silent.
explanation: Mitya stopped speaking, appearing downcast and miserable.

text: “But could you not, without in the least violating your determination to keep silent on this main point, could you not at the same time give us at least some slight hint as to precisely what sort of compelling motives might force you to keep silent at a moment so dangerous for you in your evidence?”
explanation: The prosecutor asked if Mitya could provide a subtle clue about the extremely powerful reason that compelled him to keep silent on this key issue, even though doing so was personally very risky.

text: Mitya smiled sadly and somehow pensively.
explanation: Mitya gave a melancholy and thoughtful smile.

text: “I am much kinder than you think, gentlemen, and I will tell you my reasons, and give you that hint, though you’re not worthy of it.
explanation: Mitya claimed to be more generous than they realized and offered to share the reason and the hint, despite believing they did not deserve it.

text: I keep silent, gentlemen, because it involves a disgrace for me.
explanation: He stated that he was silent because the truth would bring him personal dishonor.

text: The answer to the question of where I got this money contains such a disgrace for me as could not be compared even with killing and robbing my father, if I had killed and robbed him.
explanation: Mitya dramatically claimed that the shame associated with the money's source was worse than the act of patricide and robbery, had he actually committed them.

text: That is why I cannot speak.
explanation: He gave this unbearable disgrace as the reason for his inability to speak.

text: Because of the disgrace.
explanation: He repeated that shame was the sole barrier.

text: What, gentlemen, are you going to write that down?”
explanation: He then asked if the officials planned to record this statement.

text: “Yes, we shall write it down,” Nikolai Parfenovich muttered.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich mumbled that they would indeed record the statement.

text: “You shouldn’t be writing it down—about the ‘disgrace,’ I mean.
explanation: Mitya told them that the specific word "disgrace" should not be entered into the record.

text: I only gave you that evidence out of the goodness of my soul, but I didn’t have to do it, I gave it to you as a gift, so to speak, but you pick up every stitch.
explanation: He argued that this information was a free, generous gift from him that he was not obliged to give, but they were taking down every single detail.

text: Well, write, write whatever you want,” he concluded contemptuously and with distaste.
explanation: He finished by giving them his scornful permission to record anything they desired.

text: “I’m not afraid of you, and ... I’m proud before you.”
explanation: He declared that he had no fear of them and that he maintained his honor in their presence.

text: “And would you tell us what sort of disgrace it might be? “ muttered Nikolai Parfenovich.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich quietly asked if Mitya would explain the nature of this disgrace.

text: The prosecutor winced terribly.
explanation: The prosecutor reacted with severe physical discomfort, likely at Nikolai Parfenovich's persistent prying.

text: “No, no, c’est fini, don’t bother.
explanation: Mitya firmly refused in French, saying it was over and they should stop asking.

text: There’s no need dirtying myself.
explanation: He stated he did not need to further humiliate himself.

text: I’ve already dirtied myself enough on you.
explanation: He felt he had already compromised himself enough by sharing things with them.

text: You’re not worthy, you or anyone else ...
explanation: He insulted them by saying they were not deserving of the information.

text: Enough, gentlemen, drop it.”
explanation: He concluded with a final demand for them to abandon the line of questioning.

text: This was said all too resolutely.
explanation: Mitya's refusal was delivered with too much finality to be ignored.

text: Nikolai Parfenovich stopped insisting, but he saw at once from the glance of Ippolit Kirillovich that he had not yet lost hope.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich ceased his pressing, but he immediately understood from the prosecutor's Ippolit Kirillovich's expression that the hope of getting the answer was not abandoned.

text: “Could you not at least state how much money was in your hands when you came with it to Mr. Perkhotin’s—that is, exactly how many roubles?”
explanation: The prosecutor tried a different, less invasive question, asking Mitya to simply state the exact amount of money he was holding when he arrived at Perkhotin's house.

text: “I cannot state that either.”
explanation: Mitya refused even to provide the exact amount of money.

text: “I believe you made some statement to Mr. Perkhotin about three thousand that you supposedly got from Madame Khokhlakov?”
explanation: The prosecutor questioned Mitya about a statement he supposedly made to Perkhotin, claiming he had received three thousand roubles from Madame Khokhlakov.

text: “Maybe I did.
explanation: Mitya conceded that he might have made that claim.

text: Enough, gentlemen, I won’t tell you how much.”
explanation: He definitively refused to disclose the amount, telling the investigators to stop asking.

text: “In that case, will you kindly describe how you came here and all that you did when you came?”
explanation: The interrogators switched the topic and asked Mitya to detail his journey to the current location and everything he did upon arrival.

text: “Oh, ask the local people about that.
explanation: Mitya initially suggested they should ask the people in the area for that information.

text: Or, no, maybe I will tell you.”
explanation: He then quickly decided he might as well tell them himself.

text: He told them, but we shall not give his story here.
explanation: The narrator states that Mitya recounted his story but chooses not to reproduce it for the reader.

text: It was dry, brief.
explanation: The account Mitya gave was factual and short.

text: He did not speak at all about the raptures of his love.
explanation: He entirely omitted the passionate details of his feelings for Grushenka.

text: He did tell, however, how the resolve to shoot himself abandoned him “in the face of new facts.”
explanation: He did explain that his plan for suicide was abandoned due to "new facts" events related to Grushenka's return.

text: He told it without giving motives, without going into details.
explanation: He gave this part of the account factually, providing no reasons or elaborate information.

text: And this time the investigators did not bother him much: it was clear that for them the main point now lay elsewhere.
explanation: The officials did not press him hard on these details, as it was obvious that their main focus had shifted to another part of the case.

text: “We shall check all that, we shall come back to everything when we question the witnesses, which will be done, of course, in your presence,” Nikolai Parfenovich concluded the interrogation.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich stated that they would verify Mitya's story and revisit all the details when questioning witnesses, which Mitya would be allowed to attend.

text: “And now allow me to make a request of you, that you lay out here on the table all the things you have in your possession, especially all the money you now have.”
explanation: He then requested that Mitya empty his pockets, placing everything he possessed—especially any money—on the table.

text: “Money, gentlemen?
explanation: Mitya repeated the request for money.

text: By all means, I understand the need for it.
explanation: He willingly consented, stating he understood the necessity of the request.

text: I’m even surprised you didn’t ask sooner.
explanation: He expressed surprise that they had not asked him to do this earlier.

text: True, I wasn’t going anywhere, I’m sitting in plain sight of everyone.
explanation: He acknowledged that since he was confined and in full view, they may have delayed the request.

text: Well, here it is, my money, here, count it, take it, that’s all, I think.”
explanation: He offered his money, inviting them to count and take it, believing that was the total amount.

text: He took everything out of his pockets, even the change; he pulled two twenty-kopeck pieces from the side pocket of his waistcoat.
explanation: Mitya thoroughly emptied all his pockets, including a small amount of change, such as two twenty-kopeck coins from his waistcoat.

text: They counted the money, which came to eight hundred and thirty-six roubles and forty kopecks.
explanation: The officials counted the currency, finding the total to be 836 roubles and 40 kopecks.

text: “And that’s all?” asked the district attorney.
explanation: The district attorney asked if that was absolutely all the money Mitya had.

text: “All.”
explanation: Mitya confirmed it was the entire amount.

text: “You were so good as to tell us, giving your evidence just now, that you spent three hundred roubles at Plotnikov’s shop, gave ten to Perkhotin, twenty to the coachman, lost two hundred in a card game here, so then ...”
explanation: The district attorney began to tally the money Mitya had already admitted to spending: 300 roubles at Plotnikov's, 10 to Perkhotin, 20 to the coachman, and 200 lost in a card game.

text: Nikolai Parfenovich totaled it all up.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich added all these figures together.

text: Mitya willingly helped.
explanation: Mitya actively assisted in the calculation.

text: They remembered every kopeck and added it to the reckoning.
explanation: They included all the smallest amounts to ensure a precise total.

text: Nikolai Parfenovich made a quick calculation.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich performed the final sum rapidly.

text: “It follows that you originally had about fifteen hundred roubles, if we include this eight hundred.”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich concluded that, by adding the spent money to the 800 roubles Mitya currently had, his initial sum was around 1,500 roubles.

text: “It follows,” Mitya snapped.
explanation: Mitya agreed with the calculation impatiently.

text: “Why, then, does everyone claim there was much more?”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich questioned why all other witnesses insisted that Mitya had possessed a significantly larger sum of money.

text: “Let them claim it.”
explanation: Mitya dismissed the contradicting testimony of the others.

text: “But you also claimed it yourself.”
explanation: The prosecutor reminded Mitya that he, too, had earlier claimed to have more money.

text: “I also claimed it.”
explanation: Mitya admitted that he had previously exaggerated the amount.

text: “We shall still check it against the evidence of other persons who have not yet been questioned; don’t worry about your money, it will be kept in a proper place and will be at your disposal at the end of ... of what is now beginning ... if it proves, or rather if we prove, so to speak, that you have an undisputed right to it.
explanation: The officials informed Mitya that they would cross-reference his statement with others' testimony, assuring him that the seized money would be safely stored and returned to him after the current legal process concluded, provided they could confirm he had a legitimate, unquestionable right to it.

text: Well, sir, and now...”
explanation: The prosecutor then stated he was moving on to the next stage of the interrogation.

text: Nikolai Parfenovich suddenly got up and firmly announced to Mitya that he was “obliged and duty-bound” to conduct a most thorough and minute examination “of your clothes and everything else...”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich stood up and formally told Mitya that they were legally required to perform an extremely detailed inspection of his clothing and all his belongings.

text: “As you wish, gentlemen, I’ll turn all my pockets out, if you like.”
explanation: Mitya submitted to the request, offering to empty his pockets for them.

text: And indeed he began turning his pockets out.
explanation: Mitya immediately started pulling out the contents of his pockets.

text: “It will even be necessary for you to take off your clothes.”
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich informed Mitya that a full body search would require him to undress completely.

text: “What? Undress?
explanation: Mitya expressed shock at the demand to undress.

text: Pah, the devil!
explanation: He showed his strong disgust and annoyance.

text: You can search me like this, isn’t that possible?”
explanation: He protested, asking if it wasn't possible for them to search him while he remained clothed.

text: “Utterly impossible, Dmitri Fyodorovich.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich replied that a clothed search was absolutely not possible.

text: You must take your clothes off.”
explanation: He stated the mandatory requirement for Mitya to remove his clothing.

text: “As you will,” Mitya gloomily submitted, “only, please, not here—behind the curtains.
explanation: Mitya conceded sadly, but requested that the search not be conducted in the open, suggesting the area behind the curtains.

text: Who will do the examining?”
explanation: He asked who would be responsible for performing the body search.

text: “Behind the curtains, of course,” Nikolai Parfenovich inclined his head in a token of consent.
explanation: Nikolai Parfenovich nodded in agreement to the private location, saying it would certainly be behind the curtains.

text: His little face even wore an expression of unusual importance.
explanation: The district attorney's face showed a look of heightened seriousness and self-importance.
